reason: The single member (Maintenance > Tasks > Object existence check > Create job wizard; select nodes/volumes/consistency) is exactly this operation. A search of the StorageGRID list for exist/integrity/verif found only storagegrid/view-object-verification-result ('Monitor object verification operations'), which is a different action (view, not run). The task sits under 'Troubleshoot object and storage issues > Verify object integrity', so recovery/Troubleshooting fits.

The member page 'Configuration: cluster-admin tasks' does the following: create project-1/project-2 namespaces, developer roles, a resource-quotas ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBindings and RoleBindings. The name is slightly narrow (it leaves out the bindings), but it is accurate. The closest candidate, add-tenant-project ('Scaling: Adding more projects'), is a broader end-to-end workflow: it creates an SVM, project, role, rolebinding, Trident backend, storage class and ResourceQuota. It therefore contains this operation, so it is correctly separate. Security and access control fits RBAC work.

Two members clearly fit: 'View your subscriptions' (Licenses and subscriptions > Marketplace Subscriptions) and the API 'Get SaaS marketplace account' ('retrieve the current marketplace account and subscriptions'). The third member is borderline. 'Manage PAYGO subscriptions' (Overview tab > Cloud Volumes ONTAP tile > View > Subscriptions tab) follows the same UI path as 'View details about a specific data service' ('Select View for the respective data service (including Cloud Volumes ONTAP)... Select either the Licenses or Subscriptions tab'). That task is filed under netapp-console-platform/view-license ('View licenses and subscriptions'). So the boundary between the two view ops is fuzzy, but view-license also covers direct licenses and is not a clear duplicate.

Both members run the manual client cutover of an SVM migration. One is from the ONTAP site, the other from the ASA r2 site ('On the ASA r2 cluster, manually execute client cutover'); they differ only by platform, so they belong together. The SVM-migration ops (migrate-svm, pause, resume, cancel, view, remove-source-svm) are all distinct actions, and there is no REST cutover task, so there is no duplicate. The kind is questionable. This is a standalone action on an existing migration object, like the sibling ops pause-svm-migration and resume-svm-migration (kind=configure) and cancel-svm-migration (kind=lifecycle). It is not a reusable sub-procedure shared by many procedures, so kind=step is a stretch. The categories are also inconsistent across siblings: migrate/cancel are 'Cluster and system administration', while this op is 'Upgrade and lifecycle'.

One member is from page 'Manage network IP interfaces' and calls 'GET /api/network/ip/interfaces?location.home_port.name=e0a&fields=location.home_node.name,service_policy.name,ip.address,enabled'. That is a LIF query, not a BGP peer-group query. It was probably merged because its section title is identical to the BGP page's 'Retrieve specific fields and limiting the output using filters'. It belongs in ontap/view-lif, which already holds the sibling network_ip_interfaces tasks ('Retrieve all interfaces in the cluster', etc.). The other three members (GET /network/ip/bgp/peer-groups, all / specific / filtered) are correct. No other BGP view op exists: create-bgp-peer-group, modify-bgp-peer-group and configure-bgp-configuration are different actions.

There are four members: the Hybrid Cloud Control UI and API methods of 'Upgrade Element software', each mirrored on the element-software and hci sites. They differ only in interface and site. Related ops are correctly separate: upgrade-storage-firmware, upgrade-management-node, upgrade-management-services, verify-storage-cluster-health (pre-upgrade health checks, a different action) and upgrade-system ('System upgrade sequence', a broader workflow). No duplicate was found.

The single member is Edit agent > HTTP Proxy Configuration > 'Select Explicit proxy in the Configuration type field' > Enable Proxy > Save. The same page also yields enable-transparent-proxy (a CLI install of the proxy certificate, giving a different resulting configuration type) and enable-direct-api-traffic. Those are distinct outcomes, so they are correctly separate. The only other proxy op, console-copy-and-sync/modify-data-broker-proxy-configuration, is in another domain and on another object.

Both members are the same page on the keystone-staas and keystone-staas-2 sites: select a MetroCluster subscription and open the 'Advanced data protection (ADP)' tab. The candidate ops view-subscription-consumption (current usage) and view-subscription-consumption-trend (Consumption trend tab) are different views on different tabs, so they are not duplicates. The category matches the sibling Keystone subscription views.

The member is an overview page whose 'steps' are only links to Part 1-3 articles ('Integrating ... as a private S3 bucket into AWS SageMaker', etc.), so not_a_task/Other is right. The actionable parts are separate ops (create-sagemaker-notebook-instance, upload-file, run-sagemaker-training-job, create-aws-lambda-function, create-sagemaker-lifecycle-configuration). No other overview op covers this page.

Both members change the ONTAP Select Deploy utility admin password, one from the CLI ('password modify') and one from the web UI ('Change Password'). They differ only in interface. The recall search found only ontap/modify-user-account-password, whose members all change ONTAP cluster, SVM or FSx account passwords (e.g. 'Change an ONTAP administrator password', 'Reset the fsxadmin password'). The Deploy utility has its own separate account, so that op is not a duplicate. The other Deploy security sections of the same page are correctly split into add-management-server-account and enable-deploy-multifactor-authentication.

All 4 members physically swap a PSU ('Unplug the power cord...', 'slide out the power supply unit'). They differ only in hardware platform: SF-series, H-series, and DC PSUs in H615C/H610S. The DC variant counts as a platform variant with the same end state. A domain grep for power/PSU found no other PSU-replacement op; the 'power off/on' ops are different actions. The name is model-free, and kind=hardware with category Hardware maintenance is correct.

Both members generate an SCV support bundle, one from the maintenance console ('option 4) Support and Diagnostics') and one from the SCV UI ('Settings > Support > Generate Support Bundle'). They differ only in interface. The nearby ops in the domain (download-job-log, configure-syslog-server, modify-audit-log-settings) have different objects. kind=query is defensible for read-only diagnostic collection. However, the catalog is inconsistent across domains: the same operation is labelled 'recovery' in astra, keystone, trident and console (e.g. trident/generate-support-bundle) and 'query' here and in data-migrator.

Borderline scope mismatch between the two overview members. The FSx overview lists the full workflow: backup user/hdbuserstore, storage, credentials, 'Add HANA host to SnapCenter', policies and 'Configure HANA resource protection'. The generic page covers only 'initial' settings: credentials, storage system configuration and policies. Its resource protection is a separate page, already its own op (configure-snapcenter-sap-hana-resource). So the FSx overview is the broader workflow that contains the generic initial config. Both are chapter-overview lists, so merging them is only a mild error. No duplicate op was found elsewhere in the domain. Out of scope but noticed: the sibling section fsxn-snapcenter-config#configure-storage is filed under configure-sap-hana-fcp-storage-configuration, although it is adding an SVM to SnapCenter (add-snapcenter-storage-system).

All members are GETs on security/accounts. The SP, AD and 'configured' variants differ only in query filters (applications/authentication method), 'Retrieve the user account details' is a GET of a single record, and 'List the accounts using the ONTAP REST API' is the automation-docs version. A grep of view/list/retrieve ops on account, login, user and admin found no other cluster/SVM login-account view op. view-ssh-public-key, view-totp-profile and view-local-smb-user are different objects.

The 'Example for creating a group rule' member is a section of the same 'Add group rules' page and walks the same dialog ('Specify a name for the group rule; Select the object type...'). The fragment policy applies. Other group ops in the domain differ by action (modify-group-rule, delete-group-rule) or by object (create-group, create-group-action), so none is a duplicate. The category (Monitoring) matches the sibling group ops.

The Linux and Windows pages run the same command ('wfa --db-access=public --restart') and differ only in host OS. Both pages also offer a 'Disable remote access' row ('--db-access=default') in one options table. That row is an option inside the procedure, and the domain has no separate disable op, so enable is a fair name. The other database ops in the domain (backup, restore, transaction timeout, data-source database user) are different operations.

The single member is 'Edit local Windows group properties' (System Manager classic, Groups tab > Edit: description, privileges, members). The domain has no CLI or REST modify task for local groups (no 'local-group modify' or PATCH /protocols/cifs/local-groups in the index), so no duplicate. rename-local-windows-group is a separate rename action and not a duplicate. Minor inconsistency: the sibling ops call the object 'local SMB group' (create/delete/view-local-smb-group) and file create-local-smb-group under Security and access control, while this op uses 'local Windows group' and File access protocols (NAS). Both labels are defensible.

The single member is a section of the MetroCluster 'Complete recovery' page. The other sections of that page are also split into their own ops (switchback, restore-key-management-configuration, mirror-aggregate), so the split is consistent. The content is more than a verify: 'license show', 'metrocluster check license show', then 'Install each license key: system license add' and 'license clean-up -unused'. This overlaps with ontap/install-license, which already absorbs the analogous verify-then-add tasks 'Verify and add your protocol FC or iSCSI license' (license show + license add) and 'Installing licenses for the new controller module'. It is a borderline merge candidate rather than a clear duplicate. kind=step is also a stretch: the section appears in only one procedure, not many.

Both members are GET /api/security/key-stores examples: list all keystores and get one by UUID. This is the same query with and without a filter. The closest candidate is ontap/view-key-manager (GET /security/key-managers, 'Retrieve the key manager configurations for all clusters and SVMs'), but that is a different resource. It returns the KMIP/onboard key manager's servers and certificates. The keystore resource is an inventory of every key manager configuration (okm, kmip, akv, gcp, aws, barbican) with 'enabled'/'state' flags, including inactive ones. The catalog also keeps enable-keystore-configuration and delete-keystore-configuration as their own ops. I treat these as different objects, but the overlap is close (the keystore example's own title is 'Retrieve information for all configured key managers').

All 149 members are per-platform pages, or Option-N fragments of those pages, that shut down or take over one impaired controller (suppress AutoSupport, 'Disable automatic giveback', 'Take the impaired controller to the LOADER prompt'). They cover controller replacement, automated/manual boot recovery and boot media shutdown. The 4 chassis-replacement members (a1k, asa-r2-a1k, afx-1k, afx-2k chassis-replace-shutdown) looked suspect but use the same single-controller takeover steps. Their steps are the same giveback/LOADER sequence, unlike ontap/shut-down-controllers, which halts both nodes ('Halt the two nodes located in the impaired chassis'). These are not duplicates: ontap/shut-down-controllers is a whole-chassis halt, ontap/halt-controller-node is for controller upgrades, ontap/shut-down-controller-module is for MetroCluster FC expansion, and ontap/shutdown-node-2 is a generic node halt. kind=step matches the fragment policy's reusable sub-procedure.

The two members (local vs remote destination SVM) are correctly merged. However, ontap/restore-s3-bucket ('Restore an S3 bucket from a cloud target', task ontap/s3-snapmirror/restore-cloud-target-task) is the same operation. Its System Manager steps match the remote-destination member word for word: 'Click Protection > Relationships, then select SnapMirror S3', 'select Restore', 'Under Source, select Existing Bucket or New Bucket'. Its CLI is the same 'snapmirror restore' command, with only the -source-path changed (object_store_name:/objstore instead of svm:/bucket/name). The resulting state is identical (a bucket restored from its SnapMirror S3 copy). The cloud target is itself a SnapMirror S3 destination, so this op's own name covers it. Where the copy lives is a parameter, just like the local/remote split already merged here.

The single member edits the iSCSI service ('In the Edit iSCSI Service Configuration dialog box, enter an iSCSI alias in the Target Alias field'). 'Set the iSCSI target alias' / modify is more accurate than the doc title 'Create iSCSI aliases'. Searches of the ONTAP list for alias, iSCSI service and target alias turned up no other op for editing the iSCSI target alias. configure-iscsi-service, view-iscsi-service, disable-iscsi-service and start-iscsi-service are different actions.

The REST member ('Update the application credentials ID and secret for a specific Barbican configuration') and the CLI member ('Update the credentials and settings of a Barbican KMS configuration') are the same modify on the same object, differing only by interface. ontap/modify-cloud-key-manager covers AWS KMS, AKV and GCKMS updates only, and the Barbican create, view, rekey and delete ops are also kept separate, so Barbican is a distinct object type. Merging AWS, Azure and GCP into modify-cloud-key-manager while view and delete stay per-provider is an inconsistency, but it belongs to that op, not this one.

Both members deploy Milvus with its data on NetApp storage. One runs on on-prem Kubernetes with ONTAP NFS PVs and a NAS/S3 bucket as external S3 ('Create a NAS bucket from ONTAP or StorageGRID ... include them in an External S3'). The other uses FSx for ONTAP mounted on EC2 with docker-compose ('Set up a Milvus cluster based on the docker-compose.yaml'). The differences are platform and packaging, which the rules merge. Both pages provision storage, deploy and validate, so kind=workflow is defensible (lifecycle would also fit). No other Milvus deploy op exists in any domain; the other vector-db ops are not_a_task overview, DR and performance pages.

'Remove connection' and 'Remove a grid federation connection by force' are two paths on one page with the same end state (the connection is removed). The force path is for when the other grid is unreachable, so it is a variant, not a different outcome. The StorageGRID list has separate create, modify, view, test, rotate-certificate and clear-error ops for the connection, and remove-grid-federation-tenant-permission is a different object. No duplicate found.

The three members (bully, shark, victim) follow the same GUI steps on the Event details page, differing only in the chart filter ('select Bully Workloads' / 'Shark Workloads' / 'Victim Workloads'). This is a filter difference within one query. No other AIQUM op covers this: analyze-workload is the workload analyzer, the troubleshoot-*-event ops are event-type-specific responses, and view-event lists events.

The single member is the create procedure ('select Add Template ... Provide the requested values ... Select Add Template'). The related ops do different things: modify-config-drift-template ('Clone, share, edit or delete existing ... templates'), compare-config-drift-report and create-config-drift-timeline-report. No duplicate found.

Both members are examples on the same REST endpoint (/resource-tags/{value}/resources): 'List all resources that are tagged for the test environment' and 'List all volumes that have been tagged for the accounting team'. They differ only by a type=volume query filter. The closest other op, ontap/view-resource-tag ('List all of the used tags', 'Find tags that are being used by at least 3 resources'), returns the tags themselves rather than the tagged resources, so it is a different query. The other tag ops (assign-volume-tag, remove-resource-tag, *-fabricpool-object-tag) change state. Name, kind=query and category are fine.

'Get Azure availability zones' (GET /occm/api/azure/vsa/metadata/availability-zones, by region) and GCP 'Get zones' (GET /occm/api/gcp/ha/metadata/zones) are the same metadata lookup on different cloud providers (a platform difference). The domain's only other zone or region op is view-cloud-region ('Get Azure regions | Get regions'), which queries a different object. Name is neutral, kind=query is right, and 'Cloud and hybrid services' fits.

The console-setup-admin 'Delete a folder or project' and console-local 'Delete a folder or fleet' pages have identical steps ('From the Organization page, navigate to a project or folder ... select Delete'). Fleet is the local-deployment term for project. The related ops create-, modify- and view-* for folder or project differ by action, and remove-resource-association acts on a different object, so none is a duplicate. The category matches the sibling ops (create-/modify-folder-or-project are also 'Cluster and system administration').

All four members change a FlexGroup's size. Grouping growth with shrinking matches how resize-volume and resize-nvme-namespace are grouped, and SM classic's 'Resize FlexGroup Volume' covers both. Including 'Expand the source FlexGroup volume of a SnapMirror relationship' (volume expand, which adds constituents) is borderline but supported by the docs. increase-capacity-task lists 'Expand the FlexGroup volume by adding new member volumes' as one way to increase size. The SM classic page says 'resize ... by resizing existing resources or by adding new resources'. The source-expand page says you expand 'in the same way that you expand a regular FlexGroup volume'. No duplicate was found: resize-volume is FlexVol/generic, resize-flexcache-volume is a different object, and configure-flexgroup-volume (autosize) is a different setting.

The BES-53248-specific page and the generic 'Configure log collection for Ethernet switch health monitoring' page use the same 'system switch ethernet log setup-password / enable-periodic' procedure. They differ only by switch model. A full-text search for log-collection commands found no other switch log-collection tasks outside this op. 'Verify SSH for log collection on Cisco 9332D/9364D/9808' belongs to verify-switch-ssh-configuration, which is a different action and object. Name is model-neutral and kind and category fit.

The single member ('select SnapCenter Plug-in for VMware > Resource Groups ... Select Run Now to start the ad-hoc backup') is an on-demand backup of an SCV resource group. There is no same-domain duplicate: the other backup ops cover Proxmox, OpenShift/Velero and Hyper-V. configure-vvols-datastore-vm-protection is a broader workflow, and create-resource-group is for Shift Toolkit. Note, not penalized because recall is scoped to the domain: the same operation exists in another domain as snapcenter-plug-in-for-vmware-vsphere/back-up-resource-group ('Back up resource groups on demand in the SCV'). The product name in the label is needed to tell it apart within a solutions domain.

All five members are the identical 'Enable MPIO for NVMe devices' section (Install Host Utility Kit 7.1, open MPIO properties, add the NVMe device ID) on Windows 2012R2/2016/2019/2022/2025 pages. They differ only by host OS version. Linux NVMe-oF host pages are whole workflows in configure-nvme-of-host, with no separate multipath step op. configure-dm-multipath is SCSI DM-Multipath, which is a different object, so there is no duplicate. kind=step fits because it is a sub-procedure shared by many host configuration pages.

The ASA r2 member has two direction sections: 'From onboard key manager to external key manager' and 'From external key manager to onboard key manager'. Their intended outcomes are the same as ontap/migrate-key-manager ('Transition to external key management from onboard key management', summary: 'If you want to switch to external key management from onboard key management...') and ontap/migrate-key-manager-2 ('Switch from external key management to ONTAP onboard key management'). The difference is the ONTAP-version mechanism (the newer inactive-config plus 'keystore enable' versus the older 'onboard disable' / 'external disable'), which by policy does not split an operation. The catalog therefore holds this switch twice: once in this combined bidirectional op and again as two directional ops. The label itself is accurate.

All seven members are OS/HBA-vendor sections of the single page 'Modify queue depths for ONTAP SAN hosts' (Solaris lpfc.conf, Linux Emulex/QLogic, VMware Emulex/QLogic, Windows LPUTILNT/SANsurfer). Each changes the host HBA queue depth, and they differ only by host OS and HBA platform. Related ops are distinct: calculate-fc-host-queue-depth is a query/calculation, and configure-esxi-host-setting and verify-fc-hba-driver-setting are broader or different. Name, kind and category fit.

Every member adds a SyncMirror plex to an existing aggregate. The MetroCluster FC/IP/stretch sections say "Mirror the root aggregate:", the DR section says "Mirror one of the root aggregates", and the System Manager classic task says "click More Actions > Mirror". The differences are platform and interface only. The DR 'Complete recovery' section is the same standalone mirror operation, not a fragment that only makes sense inside that procedure. Recall: ontap/create-mirrored-local-tier creates a new mirrored aggregate, which is a different action. heal-root-aggregate, heal-metrocluster-aggregate and configure-mirrored-fabricpool-aggregate have different outcomes. No duplicate found.

Two members are identical copies of 'Monitoring the violations in your network' (config-admin and howto sites): "select Violations Dashboard". The third, 'Using the Violations section', shows the same policy violations scoped to one asset page, which is a filter difference. Borderline but acceptable. Recall: the other violation-related ops are configure-violation-notification (a different action) and create/modify/delete-performance-policy. No duplicate view op.

Single member 'Procedure 4: Add Terraform Cloud agents' ("Click Claim Terraform Cloud Agent"). Recall: add-terraform-cloud-target ('Procedure 3: Claim Terraform Cloud Target') is a different object (the target, not the agent). configure-terraform-cloud-integration is 'Procedure 1', a different step. 'Cisco Intersight' in the name is the system being configured, not an interface or model, so the name is acceptable. The name says 'Claim' while the action is 'add', a trivial mismatch.

Single member 'Configure credentials for VM guest file restores' ("In the Run As Credentials section..."). Recall: configure-guest-file-restore-proxy-vm, extend-guest-file-restore-session, restore-guest-file, modify-vcenter-credential and modify-administrator-credential all have different objects or outcomes. No duplicate.

This is a clear interface-only duplicate. This op (GUI, 'View UNIX users and groups': "Storage > Storage VMs ... Host Users and Groups") and ontap/view-local-unix-user 'View local UNIX users' (REST: "Retrieve the UNIX user configuration of a specific SVM") both view local UNIX users on an SVM. Even the object labels ('UNIX local user' vs 'local UNIX user') are the same object in a different word order. The GUI task also shows groups, so it overlaps ontap/view-local-unix-group as well.

The SMB and NFS pages are identical ("Use the vserver create command with the -rootvolume-security-style parameter") and differ only by protocol site, so they belong together. Membership of 'Verify that the security style of the SVM root volume is set to NTFS' is borderline. It is mainly a verification ("Determine the current security style... If the root volume is not an NTFS security-style volume, change the security style") that modifies an existing root volume rather than setting the style at creation. The catalog elsewhere keeps such verify pages as separate query/step ops (e.g., ontap/verify-svm-root-volume-unix-permissions). Recall: configure-flexvol-volume-security-style and configure-qtree-security-style are different objects. No duplicate.

Three members build a report from the Clusters capacity view ("click Storage > Clusters... select Capacity > All Clusters"), which differs only in columns and filters. The node-version report instead uses the Nodes inventory ("click Storage > Nodes... Drag the OS Version column"). The catalog otherwise splits custom reports by inventory object (create-aggregate-report, create-volume-report, create-storage-vm-report, create-qtree-report), so this member is a borderline fit for a 'cluster' report. The nodes, HA pairs and clusters it covers are all loosely 'cluster storage', which makes this borderline rather than a clear error. Kind=query with action=create is consistent with the sibling report ops. No duplicate op found for cluster reports.

Single member 'Remove asynchronous mirror relationships' ("select Mirroring > Asynchronous mirrored pairs... click Remove"). Recall: remove-synchronous-mirrored-pair is a different mirroring type and so a different operation. delete-mirror-consistency-group and disable-asynchronous-mirroring-feature act on different objects. No duplicate.

Both members define a new annotation type: "Click + Annotation to create a new annotation. Enter a Name, Description, and type" and "Manage > Annotations... Click +Add... Enter a Name and Description". They are the same operation across two doc revisions with different menu paths. Recall: assign-annotation (applying values to assets) and the annotation-rule create/modify/delete/move ops are different. The annotation step inside configure-i-o-density-report is a fragment of that workflow. No duplicate.

All 4 members are sections of the one conceptual page netapp-storage-vks ('Key benefits...', 'hardware models and protocols supported', NAS/SAN driver descriptions), so not_a_task is right. The nearest op, view-vsphere-kubernetes-service-overview, covers a different page (vks-overview: use cases and features of VKS itself), so it is not a duplicate. The page's actionable content (install-trident, create-trident-backend, modify-default-storage-class) is correctly catalogued elsewhere.

Single member, the TR-4931 section 'Restore SQL Server application data' (secondary SnapCenter server restores SQL data after the Windows VM is recovered to the SDDC). The only similar op in the domain is restore-oracle-application-data, which has a different object (Oracle). deploy-cloud-disaster-recovery-solution contains only 'Solution deployment overview' sections of other TRs and does not absorb this one. recovery/Business continuity fits.

The two members are the CLI and GUI versions of the same SAP HANA file-based backup ('Actions > File-Based Backup'), which differ only in interface. The other file-based ops are different actions: modify-file-based-backup-configuration (modify), create-scheduled-job (schedule), and create-database-backup (Snapshot-based database backup).

The two encryption-at-rest pages (NVE and hardware-encryption nav copies) each install '-type client' plus '-type server-ca' KMIP certificates. The two system-admin pages both sit under nav 'Mutually authenticate the cluster and a KMIP server' and each installs one half: server-ca, and CSR plus '-type client'. They are fragments of the same KMIP mutual-authentication outcome. Borderline note: the page titled 'Install a CA-signed server certificate for the cluster' actually installs a client certificate. The generic install-digital-certificate and install-trusted-certificate-authority ops are not KMIP-specific, and replace-kmip-ssl-certificate is a different action.

Borderline member: 'Managing jobs' is broader than viewing. Its steps include 'To cancel a pending job, click cancel' and 'To remove the job history, click All or All but last 24h', which are cancel and clear-history actions that no other op captures. cancel-build-from-history-job covers a different job type. 'Viewing the Annotations job in the Jobs list' is purely view. No duplicate op exists in the domain.

Clear duplicate. ontap/enable-macsec-encryption's only member is task_switch_config_cisco_macsec#enable-cisco-macsec-encryption-wan-isls, a section of the same page whose steps ('configure terminal', 'feature macsec', 'copy running-config') are the first step of the same procedure. This op's own member, the 'Verifying the MACsec configuration' section, says 'Repeat all of the previous procedures on the second switch', which binds enable, key chain, policy and verify into one procedure (fragment policy). Both ops have the same outcome: MACsec on the MetroCluster IP WAN ISLs. disable-macsec-encryption is correctly separate. The three current members are correct.

Both members set the SVM's aggr-list. assign-aggregates-svms-task runs 'vserver show -fields aggr-list' and then adds or removes tiers. specify-svmdr-vol-dest-aggr runs 'vserver modify -vserver SVM -aggr-list'. The SVM DR page's step 1 'vserver create -subtype dp-destination' only restates a prerequisite ('After a disaster recovery SVM is created, you can use the aggr-list option'), so this is borderline but acceptable. No other op in the ONTAP list covers aggr-list assignment; modify-svm (AFX/Classic edit SVM settings) is a broader page.

Both members are under nav 'Manage the snapshot reserve' and show how much of a volume's snapshot reserve is used or available. One uses 'vol show -fields snapshot-reserve-available', the other 'df', which shows the .snapshot reserve used and available. That is the same query outcome. view-snapshot-reclaimable-space (reclaimable space before deletion) and modify-snapshot-reserve (a modify action) are different operations. No duplicate found.

Borderline members: 'Generate a second S3 access key' (GUI 'Add another key'; CLI 'regenerate-keys ... -key-id 2') and REST 'Create another key ... using key_id 2' add a new key, so the user holds two valid keys. The other members rotate an existing key, a different outcome, although it uses the same CLI command and PATCH ?regenerate_keys=true call. The name 'Regenerate S3 user access keys' does not reflect the add-a-second-key members. No duplicate op: create-s3-user, delete-s3-access-key and view-s3-user are distinct.

There is one member, 'Disable the execution hooks feature' (Account > Feature settings > Execution hooks). The domain list keeps its opposite, 'enable-execution-hooks-feature', as a separate op, which is correct. It also keeps the per-hook 'disable-execution-hook' ('Disable an execution hook') separate, which is also correct because that acts on a different object: one hook, not the account-wide feature. No duplicate was found. Execution hooks run around app snapshots and backups, so the category 'Data protection' is reasonable.

The two members are the same page, 'View performance metrics for Keystone subscriptions', on the keystone-staas and keystone-staas-2 sites, with identical steps ('General > Keystone Subscriptions > Performance'). They differ only by doc site. The Keystone list has other view ops for consumption, consumption trend, timeline, assets and MetroCluster, but these are different objects. Keystone ops in the netapp-console-platform list (link, unlink, authorize, modify) are unrelated. Kind 'query' and category 'Monitoring' are correct.

The two members, from the Storage Plugin for vCenter and from Unified Manager, both do 'Import Settings > select System > select source array'. They differ only by interface. The sibling import ops (alert, AutoSupport, directory services, storage configuration settings) import different setting types, so keeping them separate is correct. No duplicate was found.

There are four members. vCenter Plug-in 'Delete an account' (Management > Accounts) acts on storage user accounts that 'control access to storage resources'. Element UI 'Delete an account' is on the page 'Work with accounts using CHAP'. Two Hybrid Cloud Control pages titled 'Delete a volume account' (Storage > Volumes > Accounts) are the same page on the element-software and hci sites. All four delete the same tenant/CHAP account object and differ only by interface or site. 'delete-cluster-administrator-account' ('Delete an authoritative user account') is correctly kept separate. No duplicate was found.

Both members are the same REST call, 'DELETE /protocols/s3/services/{svm.uuid}'. They differ only in the parameter: '?delete_all=true' in 'Delete all of the S3 server configuration' and '?delete_all=false' in 'Delete the S3 server'. The intended outcome is the same (the S3 server removed from the SVM); the flag only decides whether associated users and buckets are cleaned up too. This is a borderline but acceptable merge. The other S3 ops in the list are separate and correct: 'disable-s3-server' (a different action) and 'view-s3-server' and 'create-s3-server'. No other S3 server delete was found in the ONTAP list or the task index.

'Issue an Astra REST API call' does 'Authorize with token ... open the desired API call' from the online API reference. 'Using the examples with Bash' does 'Copy the curl example ... paste it into the shell'. Both have the same outcome, running an Astra REST call, and differ only by tool or interface. 'view-api-reference-documentation' ('Access the Astra API reference documentation') only opens the docs, so it is correctly separate, and 'create-api-token' is a different object. Kind 'step' fits a reusable prerequisite for the automation workflows.

The two members are 'Retrieve the configured public key for user accounts', a GET on the collection '/security/authentication/publickeys', and 'Retrieve the specific configured public key', a GET on '/publickeys/{owner.uuid}/{account.name}/{index}'. They differ only in collection versus instance scope, which is a query filter difference. The add, modify, modify-2 and remove public key ops are different actions. No other op to view or show public keys was found in the ONTAP list or the task index.

There are six members with one outcome, adding discovered arrays to a management tool. They come from the Web Services Proxy API ('Discover storage systems ... View discovery results'), two vCenter plugin pages with identical steps, NetApp Console ('Add > On-Premises > E-Series > Discover'), and Unified Manager for multiple arrays and for a single array. The differences are interface and scope (one array or several). 'configure-automatic-discovery-setting' changes a setting, 'remove-storage-array' is the opposite action, and 'configure-cloud-connector-storage-array' is Cloud Connector's own settings page. All three are correctly separate.

There is a single member, 7MTT 'Editing or deleting a data copy schedule for SnapMirror transfers' (steps: 'Edit or delete a schedule:'). Membership is fine and 'create-data-copy-schedule' is correctly separate. However, the name 'Modify or delete ...' combines two actions that the definition treats as different operations (modify vs delete), while the action field says only 'modify'. The label does not match a single intended outcome. This is a label issue only.

All three members generate a test trap to the configured traphosts: REST 'Trigger an SNMP test trap', classic SM 'Click Test Trap Host ... verify that the trap was received', and 9.7 online help 'In the SNMP window, click Test Trap Host'. The recall grep for snmp/trap found add-, delete- and view-snmp-traphost, verify-snmp-polling and enable-snmp-trap, all different actions or objects. ontap/enable-snmp holds the compound REST example 'Enable the SNMP protocol ..., SNMP traps, and triggers an SNMP test trap', but its primary outcome is enabling SNMP, so it is not a duplicate. The name is neutral, and query/Monitoring fit a verify action.

The two members are the root-user and non-root-user variants of one install procedure on the page 'Install XCP NFS'. Both cover downloading, untarring, copying the license and running 'xcp activate'. The XCP domain list (13 ops) has install-xcp-smb, install-file-analytics-* and configure-xcp-ini-file, and none of them duplicates this op. lifecycle/Setup is correct.

The single member 'Create a service account' ('select Create service account ... enter a name ... Copy or download the client ID and client secret') matches the op. In the Workload Factory domain only delete-service-account is related, and it is the opposite action. netapp-console-platform/add-service-account is in a different product domain, so it is out of recall scope. configure/Security is correct.

The member 'Filtering for Objects In-Context' has the steps 'Open an asset page ... Click Edit ... Click Add Widget and select Bar Chart ... Save the widget', which adds a linked, context-filtered widget to an asset page. data-infrastructure-insights/add-dashboard-widget adds widgets to dashboards, a different container object, so treating them as distinct is defensible. The name is accurate and neutral.

Both members are the same outcome through different interfaces. The ASA r2 System Manager member reads 'Select ... next to the node you want to reboot; then select Reboot', and the ONTAP CLI member uses 'system node reboot'. ontap/reboot-node ('Halt or reboot a node without takeover in a two-node cluster') is a distinct inhibit-takeover procedure that disables cluster HA and migrates LIFs, so it is not a duplicate. The borderline call: the ONTAP System Manager reboot path, task ontap/manage-nodes-sm-task#shut-down-reboot-or-edit-service-processor ('select Shut down, Reboot, or Edit Service Processor'), is filed only under ontap/shutdown-node-2. That leaves this op without the ONTAP GUI equivalent of its ASA r2 member. Labels are fine.

All members assign applications to assets ('Bulk Actions > Add Application'). Two of them are mixed-action tasks, which makes the membership borderline. task_query_assign_multiple_applications also covers removal ('To remove an application ... select Remove Application ... Click Delete'). The User Data section task 'enables you to add, change, or remove the applications'. The op description even says 'or removes them', although assign and remove are different actions and the domain has no remove-application op. This is not a clear wrong member, because assigning is the primary outcome of each task. No duplicate: create-application and assign-annotation are different outcomes.

The single member is 'Configure disaster recovery with SnapMirror' ('Configure SnapMirror replication for the PBS datastore volume', then 'In the event of a disaster, mount the replicated PBS datastore on a secondary PBS instance'). Under the fragment policy the DR-mount step belongs to this one documented procedure. The recall grep for snapmirror/proxmox/pbs/disaster/replicat in the domain found only different outcomes: configure-proxmox-backup-server-datastore, backup/restore-proxmox-ve-vm, recover-hyper-v-vm and the vMSC ops. The name is accurate. 'workflow' would also be arguable for kind, but configure matches the documented intent.

Both members list SVMs on Storage > Storage VMs. One member shows the default list and details. The other uses 'VIEW menu, select Health > All Storage VMs ... Click Filter' to filter by protection status, which is a filter variant of the same view. Related ops found in recall (view-storage-vm-protection-relationship, view-security-status, view-anti-ransomware-status, view-svm-iops-chart, create-storage-vm-report) cover different objects or outputs. Labels are correct.

The single CLI member 'Create and activate a Barbican KMS configuration' runs 'barbican create-config', then 'keystore enable', then 'barbican check'. Its sibling ontap/create-barbican-kms-configuration (REST 'Create an inactive Barbican configuration for an SVM', 'created ... but is not enabled') ends in a different state, and it is contained as step 1 of this procedure. Under the broader-workflow rule the split is defensible, so it is not listed as a duplicate. Related ops for modify, delete, view, rekey and migrate are different actions. Labels are correct.

Both members are sections of the same page. Each one is the same outcome, 'fips mode enable' with a 2048-bit SSH key, save and reload, on a different Cisco switch model: 'To enable FIPS mode and to display FIPS status on the MDS switch' and 'To enable FIPS mode on the Nexus switch'. MDS vs Nexus is only a hardware-model difference. The FlexPod list has no other FIPS operation, and the task index has no other FlexPod FIPS task. The name contains no model. Configure / Security is correct.

The two members are the current ONTAP page and the System Manager Classic '(ONTAP 9.7 or earlier)' page. Both use the same 'broadcast-domain split' parameters (ipspace, -broadcast-domain, -new-broadcast-domain), so they differ only by doc site and version. The other broadcast-domain operations are distinct actions: create, delete, merge, modify, modify-port-membership, move to another IPspace, view and view-port.

All 25 NVDIMM and NVRAM replacement pages in the task index that are not battery pages are here. Each is the controller's non-volatile memory FRU and differs only by platform (A400/C400/A800 NVDIMM; A70-90/A1K/AFX NVRAM; A700/A900/FAS9000 'NVRAM module or NVRAM DIMMs'). afx-2k/nv12l-replace ('Replace the NVRAM12-EX module, NVRAM DIMM, or NVRAM battery') is the same component on a platform variant, and its battery option is an in-page option. Battery replacements are a separate operation (ontap/replace-nv-battery), as are DCPM hot-swaps. The name contains no model.

There is one member: 'Enable ONTAP S3 client users', which creates s3-win/s3-unix name mappings and then adds bucket policy statements for S3 NAS buckets. It is not a duplicate of ontap/enable-s3-multiprotocol-access, which creates the object store server on a NAS SVM, or of ontap/configure-s3-client-application, which sets up access keys for an S3 app. It contains ontap/create-name-mapping and ontap/modify-s3-bucket-policy as steps, so it is a broader procedure and not a duplicate. Kind could arguably be workflow (two operations), but configure is defensible for a two-step page.

The single member ('Click Commit ... After committing the aggregates, you cannot perform a rollback to 7-Mode') is correct. It is not a duplicate of ontap/complete-transition-project: that operation is the copy-based cutover ('Complete Transition', final SnapMirror update, LIFs brought up), while this is the irreversible commit of 7-Mode aggregates in copy-free transition, a different mechanism on a different object. The label problem is kind=step. The policy reserves 'step' for reusable sub-procedures that many procedures share. This is a user-invoked, irreversible state change used only in copy-free transition, so it should be lifecycle (like complete-transition-project) or configure.

The vCenter Plug-in 'Create a group snapshot' and the Element UI 'Creating a group snapshot' (Management > Volumes, select multiple, Bulk Actions) differ only by interface. The other group-snapshot operations (clone, delete, modify, restore, view) are distinct actions, and create-volume-snapshot is a different object type.

There is one member: 'Analyze performance data using the traditional dashboard' (Overview > Traditional Dashboard). The only other dashboard operation is view-vvols-dashboard, which is a different dashboard and object. No other ONTAP tools version in the task index has a traditional-dashboard task. Query / Monitoring is correct.

'Restore volumes using Browse & Restore' fits cleanly. The membership of 'Restore volumes, folders, and files using Search & Restore' is borderline. That one procedure restores any resource type ('Select the type of resource: Volumes, Files, Folders, or All'), so it covers both this operation and console-backup-and-recovery/restore-file, which holds only the Browse & Restore 'Restore folders and files' task. Grouping it here is defensible, but it leaves file-level Search & Restore represented only under volume restore. No other operation in the domain duplicates volume restore.

There is one member: 'Creating profiles' (Management > Configurations > Add Profile, 'to organize configuration files'). The task index has no other profile-creation task. create-configuration-file is a different object (the config inside a profile), and assign-profile, delete-profile and view-profile are different actions. The generic name is unambiguous within the Snap Creator domain.

All 4 members are sequential pages of one procedure under nav 'Install hardware > 3040 40U cabinet' (gather tools, prepare to move, move, complete installation), so the fragment policy applies. The only other install-hardware op, install-storage-system-shelf ('Install storage system hardware in a rack'), has a different object. The name uses '40U', a rack-height spec rather than the model number '3040', so it is borderline but acceptable. Kind 'hardware' and category 'Setup and deployment' fit.

The one member's page says 'To create compliance policies, click Create Policy... select the clusters that should adhere to this policy', which matches the op. No other op among the 26 in the domain touches governance or policies. The category is defensible for cluster compliance policies.

Two members are the same 'Add a service account' section on the console-setup-admin and console-local sites. The console-automation 'Register a service' page does the same thing: 'Select the Members tab... then select the Service accounts tab. Select Add Service Account', which returns a client ID and secret. Related ops have different actions or objects: create-service-token, recreate-service-account-credential, view-service-account, add-user. Out of scope: view-service-account's member 'Get service accounts' is actually Google Cloud metadata for Cloud Volumes ONTAP.

The one member matches: 'In the Privacy exposure column, select Identify exposure. Scanning can take several minutes... review your exposure' (High/Medium/Low). No other op in the 44-op domain covers privacy or PII exposure. Kind 'query' fits, since the scan is an analysis.

'Specifying advanced options' is a fragment of the edit procedure: 'when you edit a FlexCache volume... In the Edit FlexCache volume window, click advanced options'. The System Manager classic 'Editing FlexCache volumes' page includes 'Enter a new name for the FlexCache volume', so the Workload Factory 'Edit the cache volume name' member fits. The REST 'Modifying a FlexCache volume' member is the generic PATCH on /storage/flexcache/flexcaches. The more specific ops (resize-, modify-flexcache-volume-status, prepopulate-, enable-flexcache-volume write-back, sync-flexcache-volume, update-flexcache-relationship config-refresh) each have a narrower action, so they are not duplicates.

Both members create a new configuration file from an existing one. The CLI member uses 'cp source_profile_name/configuration_name target...'. The GUI member does 'Download' and saves under a new name 'before it is uploaded'. The two differ only by interface. create-configuration-file (the wizard 'Creating configuration files'/'Creating a configuration file') builds a new configuration from scratch rather than duplicating an existing one, so it is related but a separate op. create-global-configuration-file has a different object.

The one member runs 'Disable EMS data collection by entering Disable-SmDataCollectionEms'. Sibling ops enable-, modify- and view-ems-data-collection are correctly separate because their actions differ.

The ASA r2 page is also a planned failover: 'You might need to perform a planned failover of your SnapMirror active sync relationship to test the failover process or to perform maintenance', done via Protection > Replication > Failover. It matches the ONTAP planned-failover-task. Related ops are distinct: restore-snapmirror-active-sync-relationship (after unplanned failover), troubleshoot- (AUFO not triggered), failover-snapmirror-s3-destination-bucket, MetroCluster switchover. Kind 'recovery' for a planned failover is borderline but consistent with the S3 failover op.

The one member page covers both suspending and resuming a schedule, so bundling both in the name follows the page. modify-snapshot-schedule-2 ('Change the settings for a snapshot schedule'), create- and delete-snapshot-schedule are distinct actions, so none is a duplicate. The action value 'modify' is loose ('suspend' is used for suspend-mirror-consistency-group), but the name, kind and category are accurate.
